_about: SBDC Night-Sky Simulator — data & assumptions file. Every physical constant, scenario parameter, and model coefficient the simulation uses lives here. Each entry carries value, units, source, and confidence: measured | published | modeled | assumed. Replacing this file changes the simulation with no code edits.

scenario._note: Constellation architecture. The FCC filing (SpaceX Orbital Data Center system, filed 2026-01-30, accepted DA 26-113) bounds: up to 1,000,000 satellites, 500-2,000 km, 30-degree and Sun-synchronous inclinations, shells up to 50 km each, with different hardware versions across shells. SpaceX requested a waiver of Schedule S disclosure 'with specific regard to ... orbital plane configurations' (DA 26-113), so the plane/LTAN arrangement below is ASSUMED for illustration.

totalSatellitesDefault.source: 'several hundred thousand' framing used in report figures; filing allows up to 1e6

totalSatellitesRange.source: user requirement (slider bounds, revised from 50k); upper bound = filing maximum

ssoFractionDefault.units: fraction of total in SSO family

ssoLtanHours.units: hours (local time of ascending node; 6.0 = dawn-dusk)
ssoLtanHours.source: dawn-dusk chosen to maximize sunlight per the filing's stated goal

ssoLtanSpreadMinutes.source: assumed magnitude; that SOME spread across planes/altitudes is required is supported by SSO congestion and conjunction literature (Boley & Byers, Sci. Rep. 11:10642, 2021; SSO 600-800 km is the most crowded LEO volume with polar plane-crossing hot spots), and by the filing's own multi-shell, dual-inclination architecture; the specific ±45 min half-width is illustrative — FCC filing silent (Schedule S waiver)

shellPresets.units: altitudes km, share = fraction of each family's satellites
shellPresets.source: assumed distributions inside the filing's 500-2,000 km envelope; default preset = 'spread'

photometry._note: LEAST CERTAIN SECTION. The filing gives no satellite sizes, albedos, or attitudes. Anchor: the report annex places large unmitigated SBDCs at roughly visual magnitude -2 to +4 across the population and geometries. The m0 distribution below is chosen so the modeled population reproduces that envelope.

m0Mean.units: mag at 1000 km range, 90 deg phase angle

extinctionCoefficient.units: mag per airmass (V band, clear site)

iauRecommendationMag.source: IAU CPS / Dark & Quiet Skies recommendations

launchTrain.source: Starlink train analog; assumed for SBDC scale

cameraMode.source: typical wide-field 30 s exposure; limiting magnitude assumed for a consumer camera at a dark site. Streaks use a linear chord (30 s = ~1.8 deg of orbit); observer motion and terminator drift over the exposure (<0.13 deg combined) are ignored.

referenceBrightness.units: V mag at the reference condition: 1,000 km range, 90 deg phase angle, zenith (median of the population; per-satellite scatter m0Sigma retained)
referenceBrightness.source: direct-brightness semantics per v3 review: the slider IS the assumption, no hidden baseline. Anchors: +0.5 reproduces the report-annex unmitigated envelope (-2..+4 apparent); +5.5 = strong mitigation, the Starlink-class darkening record; +7.0 = IAU CPS recommendation. Values brighter than -4 (Venus) explore beyond any plausible design and are provided as bounds only. Mitigation measures (darkening coatings, attitude control) are the engineering that moves a design toward fainter values on this scale.

skyBrightness._note: Zenith V-band sky surface brightness vs Sun altitude. Piecewise-linear interpolation. Values compiled from published twilight photometry (e.g. Patat et al. 2006 twilight sky brightness; Krisciunas & Schaefer 1991 dark sky).

twilightGlowAmplitudeMag.units: mag of brightening at the solar azimuth horizon relative to zenith, at sun depression 0-6 deg, decaying to 0 by -18 deg
twilightGlowAmplitudeMag.source: modeled simplification of the twilight gradient

twilightGlowScaleDeg.units: deg e-folding angular distance from the Sun

limitingMagnitude._note: Naked-eye point-source limiting magnitude vs local sky surface brightness. Simplified from Schaefer (1990) visibility model / Blackwell contrast data. Piecewise-linear in mu.

userLimitingMagCap.units: mag (default UI cap simulating typical suburban-rural eyes; adjustable 4.0-6.5)

shadowModel._note: Umbra half-angle derived from sunRadiusKm/earthRadiusKm/AU in code, not stored.

sphericalEarth.source: spec simplification; oblateness irrelevant at display scale

refraction.units: boolean (atmospheric refraction ignored, ~0.5 deg at horizon)

yearAnchor.units: calendar year for day-of-year to date mapping

orbitPropagation.value: analytic circular: P(tau) = P cos(n tau) + r Vhat sin(n tau)
orbitPropagation.units: model id (real-time playback; tau=0 for static snapshots)
orbitPropagation.source: two-body circular orbit; J2 and drag negligible over minutes of playback

renderCalibration._note: Aesthetic but documented. Filled per selected style in Phase 2.

clustering._note: Hierarchical data-center clustering (v3). The FCC filing emphasizes high-bandwidth optical inter-satellite links but is silent on physical clustering; this section is ASSUMED, motivated by keeping intensive compute traffic on short intra-cluster links while longer links connect clusters and ground relays. Cluster centers are placed by the same shell/plane machinery as independent satellites, so the constellation-scale distribution is unchanged; cluster count is derived as totalSatellites / satsPerCluster.

enabledDefault.source: v3 review decision: off by default to preserve continuity with published report figures

satsPerCluster.source: v3 review: 'tens or hundreds' per cluster; default confirmed at review

clusterDiameterKm.units: km (median across clusters; lognormal). Members spread along-track with small cross-track/radial jitter; spacing ~ diameter / members
clusterDiameterKm.source: v3 review: '100 m to a few km' member separation; 1 km default confirmed

resolveExtentDeg.units: deg; clusters subtending more than this are evaluated per-member (a launch train is not a knot), smaller ones as one combined-brightness object (m_c = -2.5 log10 sum 10^(-0.4 m_i))
resolveExtentDeg.source: eye cannot separate members of compact knots; combined-flux photometry standard

stationKeeping.units: boolean (clusters treated as rigid over display timescales)
stationKeeping.source: differential drift ~1 km per 10 min at 1 km radial spread would shear untended clusters; real clusters would station-keep
